# A pure js: function returning an object folds to a struct literal, which is
# checked against the interface the importer declared for it. The plain object
# carries no type name, so the declared return type is the only thing that says
# what shape it must have.
#
# The two number kinds cross separately: a JS `number` is a SNGL float, a
# `bigint` a SNGL int. The id is 2^53+1 — the smallest integer a double cannot
# hold — so routing a bigint through a double anywhere between the encoder and
# the checker would show up here as a value ending in 2.
#
# The claim stops at the source text. What the page carries is a bare JS number
# literal, which the browser rounds back to ...992 when it parses it; grep sees
# only what the compiler wrote. Carrying the value into a running page would
# need a BigInt literal, which nothing in this pipeline emits today.
[!node] skip
env SNGL_CONSTEVAL_CACHE=$WORK/evalcache

sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html --out=out app.sngl
exists out/index.html

grep 'Ada Lovelace' out/index.html
grep '9007199254740993' out/index.html
grep '1\.5' out/index.html
! grep 'charAt' out/index.html

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import lib "js:./lib"
import app "sngl:app"

const who = lib.profile("ada", "lovelace")

component main ui {
    text(value=who.name)
    text(value=string(who.id))
    text(value=string(who.score))
}

app.window {
    main
}
-- lib/index.ts --
export interface Profile {
    name: string;
    id: bigint;
    score: number;
}

function title(s: string): string {
    return s.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + s.slice(1);
}

/** @sngl-pure */
export function profile(first: string, last: string): Profile {
    return { name: title(first) + " " + title(last), id: 9007199254740993n, score: 1.5 };
}
